BiblicalUsage: çam is one of those words that sounds small and turns out to matter. It means an aroma, and it shows up 15 times across the Old Testament. In 2 Chronicles it carries the full weight of what it says, and the other passages agree.
TheologicalSignificance: To me, çam is a reminder that God means what He says. An aroma is the word He chose for it, and I take it seriously.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
